newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Volvo to make 115,000 S40/V40 in 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Volvo to make 115,000 S40/V40 in 1997.

text.p: Volvo Cars plans to raise the production of S40/V40 cars to 115,000 in 1997, a senior executive said on Tuesday.

Around 100,000 of them are aimed for the European market, while the rest will be sold in South East Asia, Latin America and Japan, Volvo Cars President of Europe Marketing Hans-Olov Olsson told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.

"Our production of the S40/V40 model will reach about 115,000 cars next year. In 1997 we will introduce the model also in Southeast Asia and Latin America. Sales in Japan will start next summer," Olsson said.
The S40/V40 is produced in the Dutch NedCar plant jointly owned by Volvo, Japan's Mitsubishi and the Dutch state. In 1996, 65,000 cars of the new model will be produced.

"We will meet the goal of 65,000 cars. Unfortunately we have had very long delivery times on the S40/V40. It has been up to 10 weeks, which is unacceptable. But in the beginning of 1997 we will be down to a time from order to delivery of three to four weeks and that is where we want to be," Olsson said.
